title: Workshop debrief and deployment checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact post-workshop playback, facilitation notes, and an ops-focused deployment checklist for the Acme Retail POC (week-of 2025-10-27). Designed for the SEs, solutions PM, and SREs to quickly convert workshop outcomes into a runnable pilot. Not a substitute for the formal delivery doc but intended to accelerate the cutover.

Summary of workshop outcomes (top-line):
- Customer confirmed two integration patterns: (A) backend inquiry routing to Redwood Hosted API for QA/canary; (B) Dedicated pool for customer-facing low-latency features.
- Primary success metric: 99th percentile inference latency <= 180 ms for short prompts (<= 200 tokens) under 95% traffic load.
- Secondary metrics: embedding recall for top-10 results > 0.82 and inference unit cost < $0.015 per 1k tokens in Dedicated mode.
- Risks flagged: tokenization mismatch on long product descriptions, client-side retry storm during partial outage, and telemetry gaps for per-route token breakdown.

Attendees (roles):
- Acme: Sarah Park (Head of Product), Leo Ortiz (Platform eng), Maria Gomez (Retail ML)
- Redwood: Priya Nair (SE, facilitator), Evan Mitchell (Solutions Architect), Sofia Alvarez (SRE), Markus Chen (Customer Engineer)

Playback: agenda items and condensed outcomes
1) 10m: Kickoff + goals (Priya) -> Outcome: alignment on latency & cost tradeoffs; agreed to two-stage rollout (hosted for evaluation, dedicated for production).
2) 25m: Integration options deep-dive (Evan) -> Outcome: prefer server-side adapter pattern; client will call a thin proxy that enforces routing and observability headers.
3) 40m: Live demo + failure scenarios (Sofia) -> Outcome: confirmed fallback to smaller quantized model on Dedicated pool; agreed circuit-breaker thresholds.
4) 20m: Data & security Qs (Markus) -> Outcome: customer needs KMS/HSM integration and audit log retention >= 90 days; Private deployment discussed for sensitive flows.
5) 15m: Operational runbook review -> Outcome: owner assignments for each runbook item and acceptance criteria.

Slide skeleton (for a 10-slide follow-up deck to send to the customer):
- Slide 1: Title + workshop date + attendees (speaker notes: recapture goals and thank-you)
- Slide 2: Executive summary: decisions, metrics, next milestones (speak to two-stage rollout)
- Slide 3: Integration pattern diagram (thin proxy, Redwood routing, model variants) (speaker notes: show request path and headers)
- Slide 4: Latency & cost tradeoff table (hosted vs dedicated) (speaker notes: highlight recommended config)
- Slide 5: Failover & graceful degradation flow (circuit-breakers, model fallback)
- Slide 6: Security & compliance (KMS, audit logs, private option)
- Slide 7: Runbook & roles (who does what during cutover)
- Slide 8: Pilot timeline & gating criteria (SLO check, data volume, budget)
- Slide 9: Open action items and owners (links to Jira)
- Slide 10: Next steps + proposed date for cutover rehearsal (ask for calendar invite)

Facilitation notes (do's and don'ts for SEs running the next session):
- Do start with the executive summary and stated metrics within the first 3 minutes. Keeps leadership engaged.
- Do use the integration diagram on-slide to walk through a sample request. Live tracing screenshot helps.
- Do call out 'what is out of scope' explicitly (e.g., full data migration, UI-level A/B testing).
- Don't dive into kernel/quantization math in a mixed audience session; have the deep-dive ready for the infra team only.
- Don't promise SLA numbers for Dedicated until SRE signs off on autoscale policies and SST tests.

Operational deployment checklist (actionable items with owners and acceptance criteria):
- PREPARATION
  - A1: Proxy adapter code skeleton delivered to Acme repo (owner: Markus Chen) -> acceptance: repo + CI stub + README (target: 2025-11-14)
  - A2: Tokenization sanity test harness (owner: Acme ML - Maria) -> acceptance: 200 product descriptions sampled, mismatch rate < 1% (target: 2025-11-10)
  - A3: KMS integration design doc (owner: Leo Ortiz + Redwood Security SME) -> acceptance: reviewed, security sign-off (target: 2025-11-18)
- INFRA & CONFIG
  - B1: Dedicated pool sizing estimate (owner: Evan Mitchell) -> acceptance: sizing doc + cost estimate, smoke test plan (target: 2025-11-20)
  - B2: Autoscaling policy draft (owner: SRE - Sofia Alvarez) -> acceptance: simulate sustained 2x baseline load; no cold-starts > 300ms (target: 2025-11-22)
  - B3: Observability hooks added to proxy (owner: Acme platform eng - Leo) -> acceptance: per-route token, latency, error rates in Grafana (target: 2025-11-16)
- VALIDATION & SAFETY
  - C1: Circuit-breaker thresholds & retry policy (owner: Redwood SE team) -> acceptance: chaos test validated, rollback trigger defined (target: 2025-11-25)
  - C2: Quality regression test suite (owner: Acme ML) -> acceptance: baseline eval on canonical prompts, embedding recall >= 0.82 (target: 2025-11-24)
  - C3: Cost guardrails setup (owner: Acme finance + SE) -> acceptance: budget alerts and hard stop thresholds in console (target: 2025-11-21)
- CUTOVER & REHEARSAL
  - D1: Cutover rehearsal scheduled (owner: Priya) -> acceptance: runbook walkthrough with SRE, SE, customer; record session (target: 2025-11-28)
  - D2: Canary config + rollback verified (owner: Evan) -> acceptance: canary routes at 5% traffic, fallback success > 99% (target: 2025-11-29)
  - D3: Post-cutover telemetry dashboard (owner: Sofia) -> acceptance: 1h, 12h, 72h dashboards for tokens, latency, errors (target: 2025-12-01)

Contingencies and escalation path:
- If Dedicated pool shows sustained 95th percentile latency > 200 ms during rehearsal -> pause rollout, revert to Hosted with throttling, open P1 incident with SRE and SE on-call.
- If embedding recall drops > 7% compared to baseline -> remove new model, route queries to previous embeddings index, start regression debug run.
- Contacts:
  - Redwood SE on-call: se-oncall@redwood.ai (primary), Priya Nair (secondary)
  - Redwood SRE: sres@redwood.ai, Sofia Alvarez
  - Customer ops: Leo Ortiz (leo@acme.com), Sarah Park

Open action log (short):
- [A1] Markus to create proxy repo + CI stub (2025-11-14)
- [B1] Evan to provide Dedicated size/cost estimate (2025-11-20)
- [C2] Maria to run tokenization harness and share results (2025-11-10)
- [D1] Priya to schedule rehearsal and invite participants (2025-11-21)

Acceptance criteria for POC success (to be signed off by Acme and Redwood):
- Latency: p99 <= 220ms in Hosted evaluation; p99 <= 180ms in Dedicated under expected percent load.
- Quality: embedding recall (top-10) >= 0.82; no regression on canonical prompts.
- Operational: cutover rehearsal completed with successful rollback test and dashboards populated.
- Security: KMS integration approved and audit logs visible for 90 days.

Suggested follow-ups (email/next session):
1) Send 10-slide deck within 48 hours with playback + diagram + action log. (owner: Priya)
2) Weekly 30m sync until cutover (owner: Acme eng lead)
3) Book SRE chaos window for rehearsal (owner: Sofia)

Notes to SEs for the post-deck customer meeting:
- Bring a small trace screenshot for the demo.
- Bring the cost numbers and show where optimizations can reduce them (batching, quantization).
- Keep the conversation high-level for executives; have the infra appendix ready if asked.

Appendix: quick checklist for rehearsal day (short)
- Verify traffic generator can replay 95th percentile pattern
- Confirm canary routing rules in proxy + console
- Pre-create rollback tokens and have contact tree visible
- Start 1-hour smoke window post-cutover before expanding traffic

End of document.
